freezeStatus: frozen after committed evidence checkpoint and before split prediction or error calculations
question: Do earlier local candidate-by-party-ballot splitting patterns improve later named-candidate vote predictions, conditional on observed target local party-vote group sizes?
estimand: Predictive transport of source local P(candidate-party destination | party-ballot group) to the same unchanged-boundary general seat and a target candidate of that party. This is an aggregate conditional association, not an individual voting transition, personal vote or causal candidate effect.
populationAndUnit: One known target candidate and comparable source local matrix in 2008→2011, 2014→2017 or 2020→2023. The primary scored component consists only of target party-ballot groups with a supported cross-election party mapping and a source local row. Equal candidate-event weights; report party/transition and candidate-mapping coverage.
orientationAndDenominators: Source row = exact party ballot group count, including informal party ballots; destination column = named candidate, informal-candidate or party-vote-only rounded conditional percentage. Target party group sizes are observed inputs only in the conditional analysis. Predicted candidate vote count for matched groups is sum(target group size × source candidate-party destination probability). Actual matched component uses target local split percentages solely for evaluation. Divide by target total party ballots for scored percentage-point units. Published candidate share instead uses valid candidate votes; report full-vote count bounds and only evaluation-time conversion to published-share bounds, never silently use the party ballot denominator as candidate share.
primaryKernel: Source-seat local rounded conditional percentages aggregated over the unique source candidate of the continuing party. A target candidate of that same continuing party receives this party-level destination pattern irrespective of personal identity; replacement/continuation status is diagnostic, not proof of transferability. No fitting or smoothing parameter is estimated. For each source percentage use its conservative ±0.005 percentage-point closed rounding envelope; multiply endpoints by target group counts. Missing percentages for positive rows fail; exact zero is distinct from missing.
candidateAndPartyMapping: Use Stage5 eligible historical party continuity for both target candidate affiliation and target party-ballot row. Require exactly one source candidate of the mapped party in the source seat and one target candidate of that party in the target seat. No inference across report-only Internet MANA, Advance NZ or Freedoms NZ groupings. Same exact full name in the same seat/party is labelled probable continuation only; a different name is unresolved rather than automatically replacement. Inherited Stage10 supported status may be shown as diagnostic but cannot admit cases. Independent/no-list candidates, entrants without a source candidate-party destination and ambiguous multiplicity remain excluded with reasons. No 2026 Opportunity extrapolation from TOP.
geographyAndScope: Only the three independently validated unchanged-boundary general transitions; matching electorate name alone does not establish geography. Changed-boundary and Māori comparisons are coverage diagnostics, not pooled fits. The lone supporting 2020 Māori local matrix is insufficient for comparable validation. Cancelled and non-behavioural contests are excluded.
missingMass: For each candidate, retain the sum of target party-ballot group sizes with no source local row/mapping as unallocated ballot mass. Full candidate vote lower/upper bounds are matched-component rounding bounds plus [0, unallocated mass]. Do not set missing contributions to zero, renormalize candidate columns, select interval midpoints as exact counts or present the full interval as a point forecast. Joint accounting tracks non-candidate and absent-target-destination mass separately.
benchmarks: Party-only: each matched target ballot group goes to the target candidate only when its mapped party matches the candidate party; same rows and candidates.

National pooled historical split: source-year general local row-weighted conditional destination share for the same source origin and candidate party; calculated from the source election only and applied to identical matched rows.

No complete candidate residual/persistence benchmark can be called operational because Stage8/9/10 coefficients are null; report carry-forward source candidate count/share only for independently comparable probable continuations as a separate sensitivity, not as a universal benchmark.
evaluation: For each held target election 2011, 2017 and 2023, use only its immediately earlier source election's splitting pattern. Target split percentages and candidate totals are evaluation evidence only. All three kernels score identical matched target rows/candidates; report interval-bounded MAE, RMSE and signed bias in pp of target total party ballots, sample/party coverage and full-vote interval coverage/width. The interval error bounds derive from closed published rounding envelopes, not arbitrary joint-count reconstructions.
forecastPipelineSensitivity: Where Stage5 has a retained additive or proportional predicted local party share, replace observed valid-party group counts by that predicted share times observed target valid-party total, using only matching valid-party rows. Hold the observed total solely as a scale in this sensitivity; informal-party, unmatched party groups, turnout and valid-candidate denominator remain unresolved. This is not a complete pre-election forecast or an operational choice between Stage5 transforms.
selectionCriteria: Operational split view requires a complete target candidate-vote mapping with no unallocated party-ballot groups or absent target candidate destinations, outcome-independent applicability, and non-worse rounding-bound MAE and RMSE than both primary benchmarks in every chronological holdout with meaningful coverage. Without that, set selectedOperationalSplitView=null and retain conditional component diagnostics. No coefficient is selected merely for an attractive sign or fit.
uncertainty: Only three comparable transitions, repeated seats, party/election-shared patterns, rounded joint cells, unresolved 2023 aggregate discrepancies, candidate identity ambiguity and party-level transfer to replacements. Do not use candidate-event iid significance or infer individual ballot transitions. Retrospective sources may be selected; winner-flag counterfactual checks computation but not source acquisition.
outputs: Deterministic evidence/contract checkpoint, this frozen specification, per-candidate predictions with matched/unmatched mass and rounding intervals, transition/party benchmark scores, conditional Stage5 sensitivity, nullable operational selection and manifests. Preserve Stage5–10 generated outputs and all raw source bytes.
